findings.title: Corporate Tax Registration Timeline Compliance per FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024
findings.issueSummary: Trade licence issue date dictates mandatory corporate tax registration deadline under FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024. Application submitted via EmaraTax requires verification against statutory cutoff dates to establish whether late registration administrative penalty (AED 10,000 per Cabinet Decision 75/2023) applies.
findings.reconciliationTest: Compare trade licence issuance month against FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024 deadline matrix
findings.legalBasis: FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024; Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023 (Penalty Item 33 - AED 10,000)
findings.unresolvedExplanation: If the licence was issued in March/April of prior years, registration was due by 31 May 2024. Confirmation of FTA penalty assessment on EmaraTax portal required.
findings.recommendedAction: Inspect EmaraTax liabilities tab to verify if late registration penalty has been assessed, and submit waiver or payment reconciliation if applicable.

findings.title: Establishment Card & Labour Immigration Compliance
findings.issueSummary: Establishment Card No. 261138997 is on record alongside personal sponsorship agreement. Verification is required to confirm whether company sponsors resident employees under MOHRE/Free Zone or operates exclusively via external personal sponsorship.
findings.reconciliationTest: Cross-check visa quota, active employee headcount, and Wages Protection System (WPS) registration requirements
findings.legalBasis: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 (UAE Labour Law); Ministerial Resolution No. 43 of 2022 (WPS)
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Companies with active employment visas must comply with WPS salary transfers. Free zone entities without MOHRE employees may be exempt from WPS but must maintain valid zone establishment renewal.
findings.recommendedAction: Obtain immigration portal active visa listing to confirm zero direct employee liabilities or verify WPS compliance proof if staff are sponsored.

findings.title: VAT Mandatory Registration Threshold Assessment & Cross-Border Advisory Income
findings.issueSummary: Entity provides management consulting services across GCC/Singapore. Mandatory VAT registration applies if taxable and zero-rated supplies exceed AED 375,000 in previous 12 months or are anticipated in next 30 days. No VAT Certificate or TRN is on file.
findings.reconciliationTest: Test rolling 12-month turnover against AED 375,000 mandatory threshold and AED 187,500 voluntary threshold
findings.legalBasis: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017 on Value Added Tax (Articles 13 & 14)
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Exports of consulting services to non-resident entities outside UAE generally qualify for 0% zero-rating under Article 31, but zero-rated supplies count towards the mandatory registration threshold.
findings.recommendedAction: Perform rolling 12-month turnover computation. If turnover exceeds AED 375,000, submit VAT registration application immediately to avoid late registration penalty of AED 10,000.

findings.title: Free Zone Annual Financial Statement Audit & Regulatory Renewal Filing
findings.issueSummary: Licensing regulations require entities to prepare and file audited financial statements signed by an approved auditor at annual licence renewal. No signed audit reports or filing submission receipts are on record.
findings.reconciliationTest: Verify licence renewal requirements against zone authority submission receipts
findings.legalBasis: Free Zone Implementing Regulations; UAE Commercial Companies Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 Art. 27)
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Zone authorities may impose fines or suspend licence renewal if audited financials are not submitted within 3 to 6 months of financial year end.
findings.recommendedAction: Engage AMRG Audit Practice or approved zone auditor to audit FY2023 and FY2024 accounts for submission to the licensing registrar.

findings.title: Free Zone Corporate Tax 0% Qualifying Status vs Standard 9% Regime
findings.issueSummary: Entity is registered in a UAE Free Zone. Under Corporate Tax Law, free zone entities default to 0% on Qualifying Income only if adequate substance is maintained, de minimis non-qualifying revenue test is met, and transfer pricing documentation is prepared. Otherwise, 9% standard tax applies.
findings.reconciliationTest: Analyze revenue streams between Qualifying Activities (Cabinet Decision 55/2023) and Excluded Activities
findings.legalBasis: Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 (Articles 18 & 55); Cabinet Decision No. 139 of 2023
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Consulting services provided to non-free zone persons constitute Excluded Activities. If non-qualifying revenue exceeds lower of AED 5M or 5% of total revenue, the entire entity loses QFZP status for 5 tax years.
findings.recommendedAction: Conduct comprehensive QFZP revenue classification review before filing first Corporate Tax return.

findings.title: Corporate Bank Account Maintenance, Signature Mandates & KYC Re-validation
findings.issueSummary: Monthly bank statements, board banking resolutions, and active authorised signers mandates were not provided for review. Annual bank KYC refresh cycles require harmonized company name and valid licence.
findings.reconciliationTest: Match registered signers in bank mandate against Certificate of Incumbency and Trade Licence
findings.legalBasis: Central Bank of the UAE AML/CFT Standards & Customer Due Diligence Guidelines
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Transliteration discrepancies between tax acknowledgment and trade licence may trigger AML freeze during periodic banking review.
findings.recommendedAction: Obtain complete bank statements for all active AED/USD accounts and confirm KYC profile alignment with bank relationship manager.

findings.title: Related Party Transactions & Arm’s Length Transfer Pricing Documentation
findings.issueSummary: Corporate group structure indicates cross-border ownership and intercompany transactions with Singapore holding vehicles. Corporate Tax Law mandates all related party transactions meet the Arm’s Length Principle and require disclosure in CT return.
findings.reconciliationTest: Test related party consulting fees against OECD/UAE transfer pricing transfer methods
findings.legalBasis: Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 (Article 34); Ministerial Decision No. 97 of 2023
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Transactions with Connected Persons and foreign affiliates require transfer pricing disclosure schedules in first CT return.
findings.recommendedAction: Compile related party transaction register and draft transfer pricing local file benchmark analysis.

findings.title: Statutory Registers of Members, Directors & Officers Maintenance
findings.issueSummary: UAE corporate regulations require registered offices to maintain physical/electronic Registers of Members, Register of Directors, and General Meeting Minutes. Only constitutional extracts were provided.
findings.reconciliationTest: Reconcile historical share transfers and director appointments with authority filings
findings.unresolvedExplanation: Statutory registers must be produced upon registrar inspection or corporate due diligence.
findings.recommendedAction: Assemble and bind statutory secretarial register bundle in accordance with AMRG corporate governance standards.
